case_name: Peerappa and Others v State of Karnataka
respondent:
State of Karnataka
Supreme Court of India

9 August 2005
Appeal (Cr.) 1146 of 2003
The Judgment was delivered by : P. Venkatarama Reddi, J.

facts: The three appellants herein are accused Nos. A2, A3 ' A4 in Sessions Case No. 30 of 1989 on the file of I Addl Sessions Judge, Gulbarga.
They, along with nine others, were charged with the offences under Sections 147, 148 ' 302 read with 149 IPC.
The accused No.7 died during the pendency of the Sessions case.
The other 11 accused including the appellants herein were acquitted by the trial Court.
The State of Karnataka filed the appeal in the High Court questioning the acquittal.
During the pendency of the appeal, the accused No.1 died.
Hence the appeal had abated against him.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in reversing the verdict of acquittal recorded by the trial Court.
Whether the conviction u/s. 302 with the aid of S. 149 IPC is clearly unsustainable.
petitioner_arguments: There is a palpable error in the judgment of the High Court concerning the provision under which the appellants were convicted.
The number of persons of the unlawful assembly is less than five.
The ground of acquittal of the other eight accused was an irrelevant ground.
respondent_arguments: The evidence of PWs 4 ' 5 corroborates the presence of each other.
There were only minor discrepancies in the evidence.
PWs 4 ' 5 have no axe to grind against the accused.
court_reasoning: The trial Court disbelieved the evidence of PW4 for the following reasons: ...
The High Court has not come to the grips of the reasoning given by the trial Court and did not critically examine the evidence of PWs 4 ' 5 before reversing the acquittal.
As regards the presence of PW5, the spot panchnama of his land coupled with the evidence of panch witness PW1 reveal that there was no crop at all in the land...
holding: The High Court allowed the appeal to the extent of convicting the accused Nos. 2 to 4 (appellants herein).
As A1 died, he was not convicted, though A1's complicity was held proved.
The three appellants were convicted u/s. 302 IPC read with S. 149 IPC and sentenced to life imprisonment.
